transformations.edit: Replaced the seed-only contract/body string recorder with an executable Verus target function, adapting the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &[T]` argument and naming the return.

Attached the generated `array_ref_view(ret.unwrap()) == slice_fixed_prefix::<T, N>(slice@)` success postcondition and the too-short `None` postcondition directly to the executable target; this records the contract under test and does not assume the target body.
Preserved the Rust 1.96 branch flow: `if self.len() < N { None } else { Some(unsafe { &*(self.as_ptr().cast_array()) }) }`; the implicit receiver is the only source syntax adaptation.

Reused the reviewed `core::slice::as_ptr` dependency shape through a local executable `as_ptr` wrapper with `slice_start_ptr`, and isolated only Verus-unsupported `ptr.cast_array()` plus unsafe array-reference dereference as named source-backed raw-pointer/array-reference boundaries.
